audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven chart rows contradicted their own why text. whys said Level 1 favours you, Level 2 is even, Level 3 swings to you, 4-5 stay yours, 6 is your dive spike and first item is even — but the rows read Skill, Shen, Shen, Skill, Skill, Shen.
audit.why: packet.levelChart matches the prose exactly: Volibear, Skill, Volibear, Volibear, Volibear, Skill, Shen. The 46.93% win rate is not a contradiction here — the entry's own thesis is that you win the lane and Shen wins the game with Stand United, which is exactly a losing win rate on a chart you dominate.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Volibear, Skill, Volibear, Volibear, Volibear, Skill, Shen, paired across both layers with ratings moved.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[6].why claimed you are a drain-tank Shen cannot burst, while the row itself belongs to Shen.
audit.why: The two-item stage is where Stand United (200/180/160s, global) converts his lane losses into map wins. That is the real late spike and it is Shen's.
audit.corrected: phases[6].why rewritten to the Stand United story.

audit.whatIsWrong: Shen's W was called 'Feint' in four places and treated as a damage shield; his Q was called 'Vorpal Blade'; his passive shield was attributed to W.
audit.why: Shen's W is Spirit's Refuge and it BLOCKS basic attacks near his spirit blade — it does not absorb ability damage. The shield is Ki Barrier (passive), gained after casting a spell. His Q is Twilight Assault. This flips the trade rule: you do not wait out Spirit's Refuge, you keep casting Thundering Smash, Frenzied Maul and Sky Splitter straight through it.
audit.corrected: Real names used, Spirit's Refuge stated as auto-attack blocking only, Ki Barrier named as the shield, and Shadow Dash's 18/16/14/12/10s cooldown made the sequencing cue.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Passive Relentless Storm' and a claim that Frenzied Maul applies a bleed.
audit.why: The passive is The Relentless Storm. Frenzied Maul marks the target and the second cast on the same target deals bonus damage and heals Volibear — there is no bleed.

edits.before: With two items you're a drain-tank Shen can't burst. Only discipline beats you now — never int the Q stun into ready CC and the lane stays yours.
edits.after: You still win the duel with two items, but Stand United banks his lane losses across the map. Close the game out before his utility decides it for him.

edits.before: - Shen Shadow Dash (Taunt): matchup-defining — His engage CC. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Shen Shadow Dash: Dashes in a line, taunting all enemies hit — his engage CC. Dodge or sidestep it.
edits.after: - Shen Shadow Dash: 18s at rank 1 and his only escape — once he spends it you own the next 18 seconds. - Shen Spirit's Refuge: 16s at rank 1, and it blocks basic attacks only, never your abilities.

edits.before: His engage CC. Dodge it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Shadow Dash is 18s at rank 1 — and it is also his only escape.

edits.before: That is Shen's favourite window — refuse it and half his win condition is gone.
edits.after: Spirit's Refuge blocks basic attacks — keep casting Q, W and E through it.

edits.before: Track Shen's Shadow Dash (Taunt): His engage CC. Dodge it. When it is down — Q-stun + all-in him.
edits.after: Track Shen's Shadow Dash: 18s at rank 1, his engage and his only escape. Spirit's Refuge blocks autos only.

edits.before: Level 2 is even because his Feint (W) shield can eat your single Q-auto trade before you have your full combo.
edits.after: Level 2 is even because Ki Barrier's shield eats your single Q-auto trade before you have your full combo.

edits.before: Once you have Q, W and E, you dumpster Shen in short trades: E slow into Q dash-stun, then W procs his own bleed while your Passive stacks. Shen's only answer is a Vorpal Blade (Q) auto-reset and W shield, neither of which wins a sustained brawl.
edits.after: Once you have Q, W and E, you dumpster Shen in short trades: E slow into the Q stun, then double-W bites while The Relentless Storm stacks. His answers are Twilight Assault (Q) and Spirit's Refuge, which blocks basic attacks only — your abilities land straight through it.

edits.before: Your R Stormbringer lets you dive under tower or chase through his Feint (W) shield window. Shen has no self-peel ultimate lane-side, so 6 is a hard all-in spike for you if you land Q stun.
edits.after: R Stormbringer lets you dive under tower or chase through Spirit's Refuge — it stops basic attacks, not Sky Splitter or your leap. Shen has no lane-side defensive ult, so 6 is a hard all-in spike.

edits.before: Level 1 you out-body Shen: your Passive Relentless Storm ramps attack speed and Frenzied Maul's bleed out-DPSes his energy-gated Q autos, so contest melee range early. Level 2 flattens out to a skill matchup because his W Feint shield can absorb your first Q-auto before you have E to commit.
edits.after: Level 1 you out-body Shen: The Relentless Storm ramps your attack speed and the Frenzied Maul re-bite heals you through his energy-gated autos, so contest melee range early. Level 2 flattens to a skill matchup because Ki Barrier's shield absorbs your first Q-auto before you have E to commit.

edits.before: From 3 onward you own the lane. E Sky Splitter slow sets up Q Thundering Smash's stun, and once stunned Shen eats full W stacks with no escape. At 6 your R turns every stun into a kill threat, even under his tower, since Shen has no lane-side defensive ult.
edits.after: From 3 onward you own the lane. Sky Splitter's slow sets up the Thundering Smash stun, and a stunned Shen eats both Frenzied Maul bites. At 6 your R turns every stun into a kill threat under his tower, and Shadow Dash is 18s at rank 1 — his only way out.

edits.before: Bait his Feint (W) shield then re-engage after it expires
edits.after: Cast through Spirit's Refuge — it only blocks autos

edits.before: Farm safely with Vorpal Blade (Q) energy sustain
edits.after: Farm safely with Twilight Assault (Q) on 100 energy

edits.before: Time his W shield to eat your Q-auto burst
edits.after: Time Spirit's Refuge to block your autos

notes: The biggest error in this entry was structural: Shen's W was named 'Feint' and treated as a damage shield in four fields, which produced the advice 'bait his shield then re-engage'. Spirit's Refuge blocks basic attacks only, so the correct play is the opposite — cast through it. packet.suspectNames missed all of this and instead flagged two false positives ('Frenzied Maul's', 'Thundering Smash's').
